method: hand-labeled expected blast radius per scenario — labels written from the fixture files + declared traversal semantics (DEPENDS_ON-style edges propagate to->from; WRITES_TO/TRANSFORMS/PROVISIONS/TRIGGERS/DEPLOYS/DEFINES are coupled both ways; REFERENCES only when it is an identity pair). Expected names are the ImpactCandidate.qualified_name forms the engine emits (domain nodes carry the 'domain:' display prefix; symbol nodes carry the bare code qualified_name).

scenarios.task: what breaks if table landing.orders changes
scenarios.notes: Pipeline landing->staging->mart. The seed is the TABLE entity only — column entities (landing.orders.order_id...) carry their own edges and are not reachable from the table seed. landing.customers joins the same view but is a sibling source, not a dependent. landing/01_landing.sql#2 writes only landing.customers.

scenarios.task: what breaks if Iceberg table lake.db.orders changes
scenarios.notes: Iceberg catalog table: archive derives from it (DERIVES_FROM), two spark.sql statements read it (READS_FROM), the glue job writes it (WRITES_TO coupled). updates_src is UPSTREAM (DERIVES_FROM lake.db.orders -> updates_src is from-side, not traversed). The meta-table orders.snapshots and source bucket are not dependents.

scenarios.task: what breaks if spark job etl_orders changes
scenarios.notes: Honest direction check: the spark_job only has OUTGOING CONTAINS edges (aggregate contains its transformations — change in the part impacts the aggregate, not the reverse). Nothing declares a dependency ON the job entity, so the labeled blast is EMPTY. The transformations/written tables must NOT be fabricated as dependents (they change WITH the job, not BECAUSE of it).

scenarios.prompt_class: PySpark job change (adjacent: table read by jobs)
scenarios.task: what breaks if table staging.orders (read by spark jobs) changes
scenarios.notes: Two jobs read staging.orders (etl_orders, views_job); mart.enriched_orders and mart.joined derive from it; the s3 mart mirror is coupled via WRITES_TO. Transitives reach the containing jobs and the enriched transformation. staging.customers is a sibling source — never a dependent of orders.

scenarios.task: what breaks if FastAPI route GET /pets/ is removed
scenarios.notes: Removing the route hits the router aggregate (CONTAINS) and the handler symbol list_pets (DEFINES coupled — the domain->code bridge), then the module + file symbols via code relations. The sibling route GET /pets/{pet_id} and the OpenAPI contract endpoints are NOT dependents of this FastAPI route (different identity, unmounted prefix).

scenarios.task: what breaks if contract endpoint GET /v1/pets is removed
scenarios.notes: Contract endpoint removal reaches the pet-store api_service (CONTAINS) and the spec file entity (DEFINES coupled). Consumer CALLS_ENDPOINT edges in this fixture point at unresolved/external TEXT targets (no cross-domain resolution in the api-only index) — so no consumer symbol is a verified dependent; the pending references count as uncertainty, never blast.

scenarios.task: what breaks if the petstore OpenAPI spec file changes
scenarios.notes: DEFINES (file -> api_service) is coupled: the file reaches the api_service it declares. The service->endpoints direction is CONTAINS (part->aggregate only) — the endpoints are NOT reached from the spec file; component schemas (#/components/schemas/*) are not entities at all (unresolved text targets).

scenarios.task: what breaks if terraform module network changes
scenarios.notes: PROVISIONS is coupled both ways: the module reaches the two resources it provisions. module.root/shared/extra declare nothing about module.network — untouched. The broken/ resources stay unresolved and out of the blast.

scenarios.task: what breaks if IAM role aws_iam_role.glue is removed
scenarios.notes: Role removal ripples through every declared dependent (jobs, cluster, sfn, policies, attachment) and — because PROVISIONS is coupled — through module.root into the whole declared estate (16 of 24 entities). The network module tree, the registry/shared/extra modules and the broken unresolved resources stay out: nothing ties them to this role.

scenarios.task: what breaks if the reusable workflow Reusable Checks changes
scenarios.notes: The reusable workflow is referenced (REFERENCES resolved) by job call-reusable, which is needed by release, which deploy needs; the Release workflow aggregate is hit via CONTAINS. The CI workflow, the external-octocat caller and the reusable job itself are unrelated.

scenarios.task: what breaks if the sql-declared staging.orders changes (cross-adapter consumers)
scenarios.notes: Cross-domain (not cross-repo — snapshot isolation makes cross-repo blast impossible BY DESIGN; this is the prompt class measured at the domain layer): the REFERENCES identity bridge links the sql and pyspark views of the same logical table, then DERIVES_FROM/READS_FROM/CONTAINS carry the blast into the etl job. shared.metrics is an AMBIGUOUS cross-domain pair (cat_a vs cat_b) — it must stay out of the verified blast.

scenarios.task: who/what is affected when contract endpoint POST /v1/pets changes
scenarios.notes: CrossDomainResolver bound sym:app.client.post_pet's CALLS_ENDPOINT to the endpoint entity (resolved) — the caller becomes a verified dependent through the domain->symbol bridge; module + file symbols follow through code relations. The sibling GET endpoint, the unresolved /v1/missing caller and the ambiguous TS caller stay out.
